failures.criterion: Sami's router design (dispatch://INFRA-490/comment/e0ed1a3b): "a pull request runs only the jobs its change needs, and nothing runs again that does not need to" — the new ci-images job runs on every change
failures.evidence: .github/scripts/ci_filter_coverage.py:727 reads `ALWAYS_RUN = ("changes", "lint", "ci-images")`, and ci.yaml:1293-1300 gives the job `if: ${{ !github.event.pull_request.draft }}` with no `needs: changes` and no filter, plus `permissions: packages: write`. So every non-draft pull request, every push to main and every merge-group run takes a runner and a queue entry for it, installs crane, logs in to ghcr.io and runs the copy, even when no row changed — and a pull-request run of it writes the package. The head's stated reason (ci.yaml:1288-1292) covers the gate, not the copy: "Reading the whole tree, it runs on every non-draft run, as lint does." Checks 1-6 of check-ci-images.sh read the tree and touch no network; only check 7, the live package read, needs the copy to have run first. The INFRA-490 architect named the shape on 2026-10-29T21:37Z: keep checks 1-6 in lint on every change, so a mirror.gcr.io reference added anywhere is still caught, and move the copy and check 7 into ci-images, selected by its own filter (.github/ci-images.yaml, mirror-ci-images.sh, check-ci-images.sh and the job's own definition), with lint able to wait on ci-images when ci-images is selected. One more fact supports the split: on a push to main that touches .github/ci-images.yaml, mirror-images.yaml's mirror job and ci.yaml's ci-images job both run the copy in the same event, which is the double run mirror-images.yaml's own header (lines 12-16) says it dropped its pull_request trigger to avoid. No red test pins this: it is which jobs a change selects, not a defect a script can read.

proof.criterion: Spec version 6 from dispatch://INFRA-333 — a fresh worker pod reads every module from the image, with no network read
proof.surface: The image's own mechanism reproduced in the issue pod: a download cache filled exactly as worker.Dockerfile's go stage fills it (go.work, go.work.sum and both modules' go.mod and go.sum in a scratch directory, then `go mod download`), then a second, fresh GOMODCACHE served by that cache through a file:// proxy with the public proxy at a dead address
proof.command: GOMODCACHE=$TMPDIR/gowarm go mod download ; then cd packages/daemon && GOMODCACHE=<fresh> GOPROXY="file://$TMPDIR/gowarm/cache/download|http://127.0.0.1:1" go build -o <tmp>/legion.bin ./cmd/legion
proof.observed: The fill is 380M by `du -sh` over 419 module zips, which is the image's own figure. The build exits 0 after exactly 92 `go: downloading` lines and writes a 100,685,180-byte binary, with no network source reachable but the file proxy. The toolchain stage's rewrite that makes this the pod's behaviour is in the image: `sed -i "s#^GOPROXY=.*#$goproxy#" /opt/go/go.env` with `grep -qxF` guarding it, setting `file:///home/legion/go/pkg/mod/cache/download|https://proxy.golang.org|direct`, so a module the cache lacks still falls through to the public proxy.
proof.negativeControl: The same fresh module cache with the file proxy taken away, `GOPROXY=http://127.0.0.1:1` alone -> exit 1, `dial tcp 127.0.0.1:1: connect: connection refused`, so the file proxy is what served the 92 modules.
